A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WaveletDiff by the same authors. All 26 pages of v2 and 36 pages of v3, including appendices, were readable. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison and matching of relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original time-series generation experiments, architectural and wavelet-family ablations, and diffusion-model reproducibility results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, EEG-related datasets, irregular-sampling experiments, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core multilevel DDPM and cross-level attention design remain intact. The specified approximation-transformer depth changes from 16 layers in v2 Appendix B.4 to 10 in v3 Appendix C.6. V3 also formulates a biorthogonal energy-loss variant and adds cubic-spline preprocessing for missing observations. The PDFs do not establish whether the depth revision reflects an implementation change or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: V3 retains the six original datasets and adds generation experiments on intracranial EEG and Sleep-EDF recordings in Table 8. Appendix C.5 also extends coverage from regularly sampled inputs to training windows with randomly missing observations across all six original datasets, adding a substantial new input-condition scenario.

E2.justification: The short-sequence comparison in Table 1 adds four evaluated comparators: MSDformer, KoVAE, TimesFM, and Chronos. FourierDiffusion, Diffusion-TS, TimeGAN, and SigDiffusions remain. The long-sequence comparator set is unchanged. These additions substantially broaden comparison beyond the earlier diffusion and GAN baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include removing 30%, 50%, or 70% of training observations before spline interpolation, generating foundation-model outputs from 64-step contexts followed by 24-step forecasts, and comparing training costs on the same A100 hardware. New controlled experiments vary wavelet configurations, architecture, energy regularization, and DTW-JS settings. The stated approximation-transformer depth also changes, while the original window lengths, stride, and training budget remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds shared-transformer and approximation-capacity ablations, wavelet-order/decomposition-level tests, energy-loss controls, DTW-JS reference-size and binning sensitivity analyses, and irregular-sampling robustness tests. New coefficient-density, kurtosis, and energy-distribution analyses investigate the fMRI/EEG performance contrast. The earlier wavelet-family and diffusion-reproducibility analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 reports numerical uncertainty using ± without specifying the repetition count or defining that uncertainty. V3 Appendix C.2.1 explicitly describes five repeated metric computations and reporting means and standard deviations; Figure 4 also displays a one-standard-deviation band. This clarifies reporting without establishing additional independent model-training runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial comparator, ablation, robustness, dataset, and runtime results. Table 1 newly shows MSDformer outperforming WaveletDiff on fMRI discriminative score, 0.008 versus 0.087, while WaveletDiff leads on EEG, 0.006 versus 0.053. Original long-sequence and wavelet-family table values are unchanged. The retained short-sequence results change only in WaveletDiff's fMRI DTW-JS uncertainty, from 0.191±0.043 to 0.191±0.011.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines primal and dual wavelet coefficients, states the biorthogonal Parseval identity, and constructs the corresponding energy penalty in Equations 30–33. Section 3.2 restricts the squared-coefficient formulation to orthogonal bases. The existing DWT, diffusion, metric, and wavelet-family mathematics otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows v2's broad superiority claim to outperforming diffusion baselines on most metrics, while acknowledging mixed results against MSDformer and opposing fMRI/EEG performance gaps. The introduction adds contributions concerning the distinction between suitability for wavelet analysis and generation, and robustness to irregular sampling. These materially revise the paper's claimed strengths and scope.

C2.justification: V3 proposes coefficient-distribution explanations for the fMRI/EEG contrast and questions Context-FID comparability between diffusion and VQ-VAE-based generation. It qualifies energy regularization as heuristic under symmetric boundary extension and cautions against comparing efficiency across different GPUs. Appendix C.3 also corrects the earlier wavelet-selection discussion, associating Coiflets with fMRI rather than Exchange Rate.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands documentation of previously underspecified choices: validation-based wavelet-family selection, explicit sequence-length-to-wavelet-order rules, DTW-JS sample/reference sizes and 50-bin setting, and PyWavelets normalization conventions. It adds foundation-model context settings, same-device parameter/training-time comparisons, and inference timings. The code-access URL and most optimizer, scheduling, and training-budget details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands positioning to spectrogram/STFT, scattering, and DCT diffusion, alongside additional recent time-series work. MSDformer, KoVAE, and forecasting foundation models broaden the comparison landscape. New neuroscience references support the discussion of wavelet-coefficient statistics and the distinction between analysis and generation. These extend research positioning beyond bibliographic metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and results narrative are substantially rewritten, and transform-domain and metric explanations are expanded. Experiments gain dedicated reproducibility/robustness, ablation, and computational subsections, with appendices reorganized around new material. The earlier conclusion and LLM-use, ethics, and reproducibility declarations disappear; v3 instead includes a broader-impact statement and revised publication formatting.

P2.justification: V3 expands the main comparison and architectural-ablation tables and adds tables for wavelet configurations, energy controls, EEG-related datasets, missing observations, and inference time. New figures display coefficient distributions, energy allocation, and DTW-JS sensitivity. The original ETTh1 and Stocks visualizations move from the main text to Appendix D as Figures 7 and 9. Existing diagrams and remaining visualizations are retained within the reflowed layout.

improvement.justification: The MSDformer comparison addresses a substantial weakness in v2's evidence for broad superiority, revealing an fMRI disadvantage and prompting a better-qualified abstract. New component and energy ablations, DTW-JS validation, and reproducibility disclosures substantially strengthen the evidence. Limitations remain: v3 overstates irregular-sampling robustness despite fMRI degradation in Table 9, and the Exchange Rate length-32 energy setting conflicts between Section 4.3 and Table 7. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in empirical scrutiny and transparency.
